boardName: Heavy periods — 7 official sources worth reading

items.title: PeriodVol — period volume tracker
items.description: Log what you used and it estimates the loss in millilitres, so you arrive with numbers and dates instead of "I think it's a lot". Stays on the device, no account.

items.title: Self-BAT — Let's Talk Period
items.description: A self-administered bleeding assessment: answer online, get a score, take it to the appointment. Run by Dr Paula James of Queen's University; discloses pharma funding.

items.title: ACOG — Heavy Menstrual Bleeding
items.description: US obstetricians and gynecologists, patient FAQ. The most specific signs: soaking a pad hourly, quarter-sized clots, bleeding beyond seven days.

items.title: NHS — Heavy periods
items.description: UK National Health Service. Changing every one to two hours, clots over 2.5cm, longer than seven days — and it opens by saying heavy periods can be normal.

items.title: healthdirect — Heavy periods
items.description: Australian government health service. Past eight days or heavy loss, around one in four affected, the link to low iron, and a nurse line (1800 022 222).

items.title: NBDF — bleeding disorders in women and girls
items.description: US National Bleeding Disorders Foundation. Treats heavy periods as a possible sign of a bleeding disorder such as von Willebrand disease.

items.title: KDCA health portal — understanding normal menstruation
items.description: Korea's official health portal, in Korean. Explains what the normal range is before what counts as excessive — a useful way round.

items.title: Asan Medical Center — heavy menstruation
items.description: Korean hospital encyclopedia. Definition, causes and the tests involved — handy for knowing what an appointment might cover.
